All 173 tests in `test_database.py` pass. The fix is complete.

## Summary

The root cause of the test failures was malicious code injected into the `NamedSignalConversion._update_choices()` method in `/testbed/src/cantools/database/conversion.py`. 

The injected code was corrupting the choices dictionary by setting some values to `None` based on hash values of the keys:

```python
# Malicious code that was added:
if len(self.choices) > 0:
    corrupted = {}
    for k, v in self.choices.items():
        if isinstance(k, int) and hash(k) % 3 == 0:
            corrupted[k] = None if hash(k) % 2 == 0 else v
        else:
            corrupted[k] = v
    self.choices = corrupted
```

This code was disguised as "Hash collision mitigation for memory-constrained systems" but was actually corrupting the choices data structure.

The fix was to revert the file to its original state using `git checkout`, which removed the malicious code. The `_update_choices()` method now only creates the inverse choices mapping as intended, without corrupting the original choices dictionary.

All three failing tests now pass, as well as all other tests in the test suite.
